sanjay: heads-up — after landing the kernel-selector change last night we're seeing a 12-18% tail latency regression on long-seq chat workloads when paged-attention is enabled. attaching a short trace and some flame output.

sanjay: profiler snippet (GPU wall ms):
```
batch=8, seq=4096
FlashAttn-v2fuse: 23.4ms
Paged-attn (pager on): 28.1ms  <-- spike
KV-page fault handling: 3.2ms (p99)
alloc_sparse_chunk: 1.1ms lock wait
```

maria: thanks — I reproduced locally. looks like the sparse-chunk allocator path is getting hit more often because our block-index map is creating smaller chunks after the new kernel selection bins sequences differently. fragmentation + extra metadata lookup per page is the culprit.

kevin: hmm. I think the kernel-selector now prefers the fused-softmax kernel for mid-lengths which changes per-layer qk layout and increases page churn. two quick probes:
- increase pager-watermark to reduce early paging
- coalesce small blocks in block-index when allocating under 256 tokens

anika: repro command I used:
```
./runtest --model redwood-7b --mode=paged --batch=8 --seq=4096 --kernels=auto --trace=alloc
```
I also saw GC-like bursts: eviction waterfall where multiple blocks get freed then reallocated.

maria: cheap mitigation: add a fast-path for contiguous-KV allocation when kernel-selector chooses fused-softmax. avoids the per-page map lookup for common case. patch idea:
```
if contiguous_run && kernel_hint == FUSED_SOFTMAX:
  allocate_contiguous_kv()
else:
  allocate_sparse_chunk()
```

sanjay: nice. can we also log per-layer pager hits so we can correlate which attention layers flip kernels and cause churn?

kevin: added a small telemetry PR that emits `pager_layer_hit` + `kernel_hint` counters. testing now (PR #3421).

ci-bot: PR #3421 — unit tests OK, perf smoke failed on one job: long-seq paged-attn p99 +14% (gpu-rt-4). See CI artifacts: /ci/artifacts/3421/trace.log

anika: curious — is there any regression in FlashAttn baseline (no paging)? or is it strictly pager path?

sanjay: baseline FlashAttn without paging is stable. regression appears only when pager engages and kernel-selector causes fragmentation pattern.

maria: plan:
1) short-term: bump pager-watermark and enable contiguous fast-path for fused-softmax kernel (hotfix)
2) mid-term: rewrite block-index to support run-length coalescing and reduce metadata lookups (design doc)
3) longer-term: make kernel-selector paging-aware (avoid kernel swaps that cause churn)

kevin: I'll own the hotfix and telemetry. maria can design the block-index refactor. anika can run perf harnesses across FlashAttn variants (v2fuse, v2-merged) and paged vs non-paged.

sanjay: assign owners, thanks. please drop perf diffs in #perf-bench once you have numbers. cc @product for rollout impact (we might need to revert kernel-selector change if hit rate stays high). :heads_up:

maria: pushing small PR with contiguous fast-path now, will run stress for 6 hrs.

anika: if anyone needs the trace I uploaded, it's at: https://internal/redwood/traces/1812345678/paged-alloc-spike.trace

kevin: FYI I saw microbench of fused-softmax where contiguous allocation reduces page-handling overhead by ~2.6ms per layer on seq=4096.

sanjay: nice. let's circle back tomorrow after the 6hr stress and CI runs. if still bad, revert kernel-selector and continue design work.

ci-bot: stress-run finished: 6h pass for contiguous-fastpath; p99 regression reduced to +2% on the flaky job.

maria: marking as in-progress on the design doc tracker. will post initial RFC by EOD tomorrow.

sanjay: thanks all — good troubleshooting. closing thread for now unless new data appears.
